plain.text: "Why, LORD, do you stand far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?" The psalmist describes wicked people who proudly hunt down the weak. They boast about their desires and do not seek God; in their thoughts there is no room for God. They say, "Nothing will ever shake me." Their mouths are full of lies and threats. They lie in wait like a lion to catch the helpless. They think, "God has forgotten; he will never see."

"Arise, LORD! Lift up your hand, O God. Do not forget the helpless." Why do the wicked think God will not call them to account? "But you, God, see the trouble of the afflicted; you consider their grief." The victims commit themselves to God, the helper of the fatherless. The psalmist asks God to break the power of the wicked.

"The LORD is King forever and ever." "You, LORD, hear the desire of the afflicted; you encourage them, and you listen to their cry, defending the fatherless and the oppressed, so that mere earthly mortals will never again strike terror."

summary.bigIdea: When God seems far away and the wicked seem to win, the psalmist trusts that God sees, hears and defends the helpless.
points: The psalmist honestly asks, "Why, O LORD, do You stand far off?"
The wicked think God doesn't see, but God sees every trouble and grief.
The LORD is King forever and defends the fatherless and oppressed.
summary.reflection: The psalm starts by asking why God seems far away. Have you ever felt that? This psalm shows you can say so to God.
